prompt: Look at the sequence $3,\ 7,\ 11,\ 15,\ \dots$ What is the next term?
hint: Check what happens from one term to the next. Is it the same jump every time?

hints.text: Check what happens from one term to the next. Is it the same jump every time?
The differences are $7 - 3 = 4$, $11 - 7 = 4$, and $15 - 11 = 4$, so the rule adds $4$ each step. Apply it to the last term.
Adding once more gives $15 + 4 = 19$, so the next term is $19$.

explanation: A sequence is an ordered list that follows a rule, so first find the rule.
The gaps between terms are $4, 4, 4$, the same each time, so this sequence is ARITHMETIC.
Continuing the rule from the last term gives $15 + 4 = 19$.

alternativeExplanations.title: A gap table
steps: Write the terms in one row: 3, 7, 11, 15.
Write the gaps underneath, between the terms: 4, 4, 4.
A row of identical gaps means "add 4 forever", so the next term is 15 + 4 = 19.

alternativeExplanations.title: Hops on a number line
steps: Picture a number line and start at 3.
Each term is one hop of the same size to the right, landing on 7, 11, then 15.
One more hop of 4 lands you on 19.
